clue.text: Cheats in bridge after bid by opposing players

indicators.note: after places the bridge piece behind the bid piece in the answer

parts.note: in the card game bridge a double is a call made by an opponent of the side that bid last
to bridge something is to cross it, so the verb gives crosses

explanation.surface: A card player suspects the opponents of cheating in a game of bridge after an unexpected bid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' sets the crossing word behind the bid. Bridge is a card game in which 'double' is a call that only an opponent can make.
explanation.definitionFit: To betray someone you appear to be helping is to play them false, a synonym of cheating them.

clue.text: Game birds

definitions.meaning: a pastime of skimming flat stones across water so they bounce
male and female wildfowl of the mallard kind

explanation.definitionFit: The stone-skimming pastime takes its name from waterfowl, so one phrase covers both the game and the drakes and their mates.

clue.text: Sort of nut that is given free

indicators.note: sort, as a verb, means arrange, so the letters of the word nut are put in a new order

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, Latin for that is

explanation.surface: A puzzled mechanic asks what kind of nut can be released.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sort of' looks like a vague description of the nut but is the anagram signal, turning NUT into UNT.
explanation.definitionFit: To loosen a knot or bond is to set it free, so the verbs match.

clue.text: Appear inanimate before the public

parts.note: describes a dead dignitary's body displayed for mourners to file past, lifeless yet seen by everyone

explanation.definitionFit: A dead monarch or statesman displayed in a public hall for mourners is lifeless and on show to the people.

clue.text: Worry about horse butchery

indicators.note: about means going round, so the worry word is placed around the horse word

parts.note: care, as in cares and woes, means worry
a nag is an old horse

explanation.surface: Anxiety over a horse being slaughtered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' signals a container here, not a topic: the worry word wraps round the horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Butchery in its figurative sense is wholesale slaughter, which is what the answer names.

clue.text: City heels underwriting gold

indicators.note: in a down clue, writing one piece under another puts it after that piece

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold
a ship that heels tilts, so heels means leans

explanation.surface: Financiers in a city back the gold market with rogues.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heels' looks like scoundrels but is the verb for tilting. 'underwriting' puts LEANS below OR in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: The French city on the Loire, famed for Joan of Arc, is a named example of a city.

clue.text: The total money that's needed for drainage

parts.note: a sum is a total
p stands for penny or pence, a coin of British money

explanation.surface: A council asks how much money must be spent on fixing the drains.
explanation.walkthrough: P is the abbreviation for a British penny.
explanation.definitionFit: A pit or well where waste liquid collects is a fixture of any drainage system.

clue.text: It's used to lift small amounts from cellar

definitions.text: It's used to lift small amounts from cellar

parts.words: It's used to lift small amounts from cellar
parts.note: cellar suggests wine stored underground, but here it is the little dish on a dining table for seasoning, and a tiny utensil takes pinches out of it

explanation.definitionFit: A table salt cellar is served with a tiny ladle for taking out pinches of seasoning.

clue.text: Person typically putting piece in the way

parts.note: a man is a piece in chess or draughts
taken as written
taken as written
a street is a way, as in a road name

explanation.surface: Someone is blocking a road by setting down a lump of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'piece' looks like a chunk or lump; it is a playing piece, a MAN in chess or draughts.
explanation.definitionFit: The ordinary average citizen is the typical person whose views pollsters seek.

clue.text: Main church mouse catcher — he turned fat

parts.note: a cat catches mice
taken as written

indicators.note: turned means the word for fat is read backwards

parts.note: lard is pig fat

explanation.surface: A cat in a church was such a good mouser that it grew fat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' reverses LARD to give DRAL.
explanation.definitionFit: The principal church of a diocese, holding the bishop's throne, is the main church of its area.

clue.text: Country taking part in formal talks

indicators.note: taking part in says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A nation joins an official round of negotiations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking part in' signals the hidden run: forMAL TAlks.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mediterranean island republic is a sovereign nation.

clue.text: Polish is considered hard to comprehend

indicators.note: comprehend in its old sense of include or contain, so the considered word holds the hard letter

parts.note: something that is seen as good is considered good
h is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Someone finds a Polish text tough to understand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' looks like the nationality but is the shine. 'to comprehend' means to contain, putting H inside SEEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A gleam or lustre on a surface is the polish it shows, both as nouns.

clue.text: A means to get off

parts.note: a way is a means or method

explanation.surface: Someone asks how to escape.
explanation.definitionFit: Off and its synonym both mean departed or absent, as in 'she's off' or gone.

clue.text: Wine with the best flavour in test

indicators.note: the wine word sits inside the letters of the word test to make the tasting word, so taking test away leaves it

parts.note: tastiest means with the best flavour
taken as written

explanation.surface: The finest-tasting wine at a tasting competition.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads backwards in spirit: put the wine 'in' TEST and you get TASTIEST, so removing T...EST from TASTIEST leaves ASTI.
explanation.definitionFit: The sparkling Piedmont white named after its town is a type of wine.

clue.text: Instrument for amplifying one note included by new composer

indicators.note: included by means the one and note letters are taken inside the rearranged letters
new means the letters of the word composer are made into something fresh

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
C is a musical note

explanation.surface: A young composer has one note for a musical instrument that amplifies sound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges COMPOSER as MROSCOPE; 'included by' puts IC after its M. 'amplifying' suggests sound but means magnifying.
explanation.definitionFit: The laboratory device magnifies tiny objects, amplifying their apparent size.

clue.text: One may be at a man's throat —-or show affection and attachment

definitions.text: One may be at a man's throat

parts.note: to neck is to kiss and cuddle
a tie is a bond or attachment

explanation.surface: Someone may go for a man's throat, or else hug and embrace him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at a man's throat' suggests an attack but means worn at the collar.
explanation.definitionFit: A strip of cloth knotted at the collar sits at the wearer's throat.

clue.text: Bamboozled inexperienced competitor

parts.note: conned means bamboozled; con, as an adjective-like stem, gives the trick
tender years are inexperienced ones

explanation.surface: A naive entrant was fooled.
explanation.definitionFit: A rival vying for a title is one who competes for it.

clue.text: Initial odds unacceptable, entering home stretch

indicators.note: entering means the home word goes inside the other pieces

parts.note: SP, starting price, is the odds offered at the start of a horse race
out, as in 'that's out', means not allowed
in means at home

explanation.surface: A punter finds the opening odds poor as the horses enter the final straight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'home stretch' reads as the final straight of a racecourse, but 'home' is its own piece and 'stretch' is the definition, a verb meaning prolong. SP means starting price.
explanation.definitionFit: To prolong something, making it last longer, is to stretch it out.

clue.text: Gives fellow a deposit back

parts.note: a don is a university fellow

indicators.note: back means the deposit word is read backwards

parts.note: to set something down is to deposit it

explanation.surface: A fellow hands over a deposit to get it back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses SET to give TES.
explanation.definitionFit: To make a gift to charity is to give, in the same tense.

clue.text: Form lessons without boys

indicators.note: to form is to shape, so the letters of lessons are shaped into a new word

explanation.surface: A school class has lessons with no boys present.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Form' looks like a school class but signals rearranging LESSONS.
explanation.definitionFit: Having no male children, a parent lacks sons and so is without boys.

clue.text: Vault supplied with English gin

parts.note: to spring is to vault or leap

explanation.surface: A drinks cellar stocked with English gin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vault' suggests a cellar but is a leap; 'gin' is not the drink but a trap for game.
explanation.definitionFit: A gin, short for engine, is a snare for catching game, and so is a noose-trap of this name.

clue.text: A pear is taken, originally alternatively, as a ripe plant

indicators.note: alternatively means the letters can be put in another way, so the words as a ripe are rearranged

explanation.surface: A pear may be picked early or left as a ripe fruit plant.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is double: 'A pear is' also rearranges to the answer, the setter offering two anagrams, one 'originally' and one 'alternatively'.
explanation.definitionFit: Meadowsweet and its shrubby relatives belong to this genus of flowering plants in the rose family.

clue.text: A highly incomplete state

indicators.note: incomplete means the last letter of the highly word is missing

parts.note: very means highly, as in very good

explanation.surface: A political region not quite fully formed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'state' looks like a nation but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To declare firmly is to state or assert, both verbs.

clue.text: Diligent worker, one in the opposition

parts.note: the ant is the proverbial hard worker
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A hard-working member of an opposition party.
explanation.definitionFit: Being against something puts one in the opposition camp, as an opposed adjective.

clue.text: An expedient move

definitions.meaning: a trick or dodge for getting by, as in 'make the answer
to transfer from one place to another

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a stratagem for coping and a change of position.

clue.text: Currently favoured over an egghead — that's fatuous

indicators.note: in a down clue, over puts the favoured piece above what follows

parts.note: something in fashion is in
read as egg's head, the first letter of egg

explanation.surface: A fashionable clown outshines an intellectual, and it's silly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'egghead' looks like an intellectual; read as the head of 'egg' it gives E. 'over' puts IN above AN E.
explanation.definitionFit: Silly and pointless remarks are fatuous, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Idle characters found a place selling convenience food

indicators.note: found means set up anew, so the letters of the word idle are cast into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Lazy people discovered a takeaway shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found' looks like discovered but means establish, rearranging IDLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A delicatessen sells ready-to-eat cooked meats and salads.

clue.text: Taking directions, expected To invest

parts.note: E and N, east and north, are compass directions
due means expected, as in the train is due

explanation.surface: Someone takes advice and is expected to put money into shares.
explanation.walkthrough: 'invest' suggests finance but means to endow or clothe with a quality.
explanation.definitionFit: To invest someone with a quality is to endow or furnish them with it.

clue.text: Fancy a bloater cooked by English

indicators.note: cooked means the letters of a bloater are prepared into a new shape

explanation.surface: Someone wants a smoked herring cooked the English way.
explanation.walkthrough: A bloater is a smoked herring. 'Fancy' looks like a verb meaning want but is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Ornate and intricately detailed things are fancy.

clue.text: Restoration of control, say, wanted in hearing

parts.note: a rein controls a horse
to state is to say

indicators.note: in hearing means the wanted word is spoken, its sound matching different letters

parts.note: meant, as in 'I meant to', means intended or wanted

explanation.surface: Restoring command is something people want to hear announced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in hearing' turns MEANT into MENT by its sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Putting someone back in a former post is a restoration of them.
